rationale: Both candidates independently nail the two most significant GT-confirmed bugs (v2-tokenizer-swallows-legacy-checkpoint at modeling_moss_tts_codec.py, and the NPU dummy-run missing seq_token_counts) with precise, well-grounded line citations, and both partially but not exactly match linyueqian's High slot-leak-on-abort concern via different specific mechanisms. Both miss the ceil/floor latent bug, the cumulative/delta chunk_np re-slice bug, and the smaller cleanup/generalization questions, keeping recall roughly tied and modest for both. X edges ahead on usefulness: it reads as a coherent, prioritized human-style review (verdict/blocking/should-fix/minor/tests) with several additional well-reasoned, concretely actionable findings (hardcoded sampling retune, KV-cache memory-profiling timing, dead-code output dict, stop-token hardcoding) beyond the shared hits, while Y's more terse evidence-dump format, despite its useful self-verification of claims, is slightly less actionable as a reviewer artifact.
